correctness.rationale: For a>-1, the Beta integral B(n+a+1,m+1) gives the monomial norm and a complete orthogonal basis. The generating-series rational kernel has numerators P1 and P2, whose coefficients were independently reconstructed and checked against Beta reciprocals in 432 exact rational assertions. For P1, coefficient signs, N(1)=2 and discriminant 4(1-t^2) yield exactly one possible negative disk zero iff t<1/sqrt(2). For P2, the discriminant -216t(t-1)^2(t+1)(t+2)^2 is strictly negative for t!=1, so there is one real root and a conjugate pair. At t<1 coefficient signs imply the real root is negative; Vieta plus r<(t+2)/(1-t) forces the nonreal roots strictly outside. At t>1 the real root lies between 1 and (t+2)/(t-1), and Vieta forces the other two outside. The threshold test P2(-1)=2(2t+1)(2t^2+2t-3) is exact, and equality is excluded by the open disk. Root-locations beyond the rational checker follow from these global arguments, not samples. Potential limitation: none found in the explicitly bounded m=1,2 statement.

originality.rationale: The searched primary works give general radial-kernel methodology and zero existence/finiteness but no identified fixed-family exact origin-singularity threshold for both first Jacobi boundary orders. The two highly similar published radial zero-freeness results address (i) 1-q|z|^(2gamma) without an origin singularity, and (ii) genuine Euclidean boundary distance (1-|z|)^v without the origin factor. Their special nonsingular limiting case is credited as prior, not claimed as new. Closest source formulas were compared at the level of their weight domains and statements. Historical priority remains provisional because a classical generalized Eulerian/hypergeometric root-location theorem might subsume the calculation.

value.rationale: The Lu Qi-Keng property (zero-freeness of reproducing kernels) is a natural structural question for analytic Hilbert spaces, not an arbitrary numeric sample. For the first two Jacobi boundary orders the theorem supplies a complete all-real-parameter exact classification, unique negative-real zero when present, strict exclusion of every other disk root, and two distinct sharp critical exponents. It quantifies the interaction between an integrable origin singularity and a boundary-zero factor, in contrast to the classical zero-free a=0 kernels. Beyond the verified domain m=1,2 no general classification or application is claimed.
